decisions.latin: Miserére mei, Deus · crea in me, Deus · Deus, Deus salútis meæ · Deus, non despícies
decisions.why: The vocative *Deus* has been bare in every finished psalm (16:6, 21:21, 24:22, 42:1, 43:10, 47:10–11: *Julgai-me, Deus*, *Acolhemos, Deus*); the glossary gives *ó* only where the Latin has *o*, and 44:7 took *ó Deus* only because the psalm says *tu* and the vocative had to be marked. The incipit *Tende piedade de mim, ó Deus* is the sound many Brazilians know, but that is memory, not a witness, and the psalter would then say *Deus* two ways. Ruled bare, in all four places at once.

options.label: Deus (bare)
options.note: Ruling; the psalter's practice so far (47:10, 42:1 …).

options.label: ó Deus
options.note: MS1932 and DM1962 *ó Deus* in 3a, 12, 19; more solemn at the incipit; adds a syllable in four places and breaks with the finished psalms.

decisions.why: The Latin says the mercy twice with two words, *misericórdia* (3a, ἔλεος) and *miseratiónes* (3b, οἰκτιρμοί), a pair the Greek has too, so by D15's test they stay two. The open row *miseratiónes → compaixões* has already been applied beside *misericórdias* in 24:6 and passed the Latinist twice. multitúdo → *multidão* (row, 5:7b).

options.label: compaixões
options.note: Ruling; the row (118:77, 24:6).

options.label: misericórdias
options.note: merges the two Latin words (as MS1932 nearly does, *clemências*) — the Greek keeps them apart.

options.label: clemências
options.note: MS1932; a word of courts and pardons, bookish in the plural.

decisions.why: *Ámplius* is 'more, further' (ἐπὶ πλεῖον): wash me yet more. DRB 'Wash me yet more', MS1932 *Lava-me mais e mais*. The imperative goes first, as Portuguese wants, and the adverb follows it. *ainda mais* says 'yet more' in two plain words; *mais e mais* doubles a word the Latin has once. The Lauds antiphon *Ámplius lava me, Dómine, ab injustítia mea* reads with the same opening.

options.label: Lavai-me ainda mais
options.note: Ruling; DRB 'yet more'.

options.label: Lavai-me mais e mais
options.note: MS1932; the doubling is his, not the Latin's.

options.label: Lavai-me inteiramente
options.note: DM1962 (from the Hebrew, 'thoroughly'); the Latin's degree becomes completeness. Refused.

decisions.latin: a peccáto meo munda me · et mundábor
decisions.why: The open row *mundáre → purificar* (18:13, 18:14b) named these two places, and said *limpar* was the fall-back if Ps 50 needed it. It does not: the psalm has the root three times — *munda me* (4), *mundábor* (9), *cor mundum* (12) — and *purificai-me … serei purificado … coração puro* keeps the echo in Portuguese, where *limpar … limpo … puro* would break it at the most famous of the three. The collision the row feared (11:7 *purgátum → purificada*) does not arise here.

options.label: purificai-me / serei purificado
options.note: Ruling; the row; MS1932 *purifica-me … serei purificado*; echoes *puro* (50:12).

options.label: limpai-me / ficarei limpo
options.note: the row's fall-back (DRB 'cleanse'; DM1962 *serei limpo*); plainer, shorter in 50:9, but loses the echo with *coração puro*.

decisions.latin: et a peccáto meo munda me · et omnes iniquitátes meas dele
decisions.why: Both second cola put the imperative last (*a peccáto meo munda me*, *omnes iniquitátes meas dele*), a chiasm against the verb-first colon before them. D2 lets order follow the ear; the verb-first order is how a Brazilian asks, and it ends each colon on a paroxytone (*pecado*, *iniquidades*). The Preces say 50:11b alone as a response (*R. Et omnes iniquitátes meas dele*): *E apagai todas as minhas iniquidades* stands alone.

options.label: verb first
options.note: Ruling; MS1932 has both so.

options.label: the Latin's chiasm
options.note: the Latin's order; sayable in 50:4, stiff in 50:11.

decisions.latin: et peccátum meum contra me est semper
decisions.why: *contra* here is the old local sense, 'over against, facing' (L&S's first sense of the adverb and preposition), and the Greek is ἐνώπιόν μου, 'before me'. In Portuguese *contra mim* is heard only as hostility ('my sin is against me') — a sense the Greek excludes and the Latin does not need. DRB 'before me', MS1932 *diante de mim*. The same words close the Pent01-3 versicle (*et delíctum meum contra me est semper*).

options.label: diante de mim
options.note: Ruling; DRB, MS1932, the Greek.

options.label: contra mim
options.note: the cognate; heard as 'against me', which is the Latin's secondary sense, not this verse's.

decisions.why: The dative of the one sinned against → *contra vós*; *soli* must attach to *vós*, not to the speaker. *Só contra vós pequei* puts *só* where it can only mean 'against you alone', in five syllables against the Latin's seven, and reads alone as the Thursday Lauds antiphon (*Tibi soli peccávi, Dómine, miserére mei*). *Pequei contra vós só* dangles; *Contra vós só pequei* can be heard 'against you I only sinned'.

options.label: Só contra vós pequei
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: Contra vós somente pequei
options.note: the Latin's order (the pronoun first); *somente* is heavier.

options.label: Pequei contra vós só
options.note: MS1932's order (*Pequei contra ti só*); ends on a dangling *só*.

decisions.latin: ut justificéris in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum judicáris
decisions.why: St Paul quotes this colon word for word in Rom 3:4 (Clementine, `consult/bolls-VULG-45-3.json`: *Ut justificeris in sermonibus tuis: et vincas cum judicaris*), so the Latin's verb, a theological word, stays: *justificado*. *reconhecido justo* (MS1932 *encontrado justo*) explains it. sermo → *palavra* (D15). *cum judicáris* is a present passive ('when you are judged', ἐν τῷ κρίνεσθαί σε); Portuguese says a general 'when' with the future subjunctive, *quando fordes julgado* — mood and tense are grammar (D2); DRB 'when thou art judged', MS1932 *quando fores julgado*.

options.label: justificado
options.note: Ruling; the Latin's (and Rom 3:4's) verb; DRB 'justified'.

options.label: reconhecido justo
options.note: explains the verb (MS1932 *encontrado justo*); the reader crossing to Rom 3:4 would lose it.

decisions.why: The two verses open alike and must stay alike (rule 6). 53:6 rendered this very phrase *Pois eis que* (ecce → *eis*, enim → *pois*, both rows), and it is copied. MS1932 and DRB keep both words ('For behold'); dropping *pois* loses the link to 50:6 the Latin makes.

options.label: Pois eis que
options.note: Ruling; = 53:6.

options.label: Eis que
options.note: MS1932 (he drops *enim*); lighter, loses a word.

decisions.latin: incérta et occúlta sapiéntiæ tuæ manifestásti mihi
decisions.why: *incérta* (ἄδηλα) is what is not known for certain, the unclear; *occúlta* (κρύφια) the hidden. The cognates keep both Latin words; *incertas* risks being heard as 'doubtful', but the Latin runs the same risk and the next word (*ocultas*) steers it. The neuter plurals take a noun (*coisas*), as 16:14b *abscóndita → coisas escondidas*. The Latin puts the objects first and the verb last; the draft keeps that, so that the colon ends on the revealing — Portuguese allows it in a solemn sentence, and *me manifestastes* is a clean paroxytone cadence. MS1932 *o segredo e o mistério* paraphrases.

options.label: objects first, verb last

forms.incerta: as coisas incertas e ocultas da vossa sabedoria me manifestastes

options.note: Ruling; the Latin's order.

options.label: verb first

forms.incerta: manifestastes-me as coisas incertas e ocultas da vossa sabedoria

options.note: natural order; ends on *sabedoria*; the enclisis at the head of the colon is formal.

options.label: obscuras e ocultas

forms.incerta: as coisas obscuras e ocultas da vossa sabedoria me manifestastes

options.note: the Greek's 'unclear' without the risk of 'doubtful'; not the Latin's word.

options.label: o segredo e o mistério

forms.incerta: me revelastes o segredo e o mistério da vossa sabedoria

options.note: MS1932; paraphrase. Refused.

decisions.why: Two futures with an object pronoun, each heading a colon. The mesóclise *Aspergir-me-eis … lavar-me-eis* is correct and bookish (rule 5); the Brazilian way is the subject named and the pronoun before the verb — the precedent is 17:44 *Vós me arrancareis* and 30:5 *Vós me tirareis*. The subject is named in both cola so that each stands by itself: the verse is the Asperges antiphon (*Aspérges me, Dómine, hyssópo …*, Ordo/Prayers) and is sung alone. The Latin is a future, not an imperative, and stays one. hyssópus → *hissopo* (the current spelling; MS1932 *hissope*).

options.label: Vós me aspergireis … vós me lavareis

forms.asperges: Vós me aspergireis com o hissopo

options.label: mesóclise
options.note: the Latin's verb-first order; correct, bookish.

options.label: second subject dropped

forms.asperges: Vós me aspergireis com o hissopo

options.note: one syllable shorter; a colon opening on an unstressed *me*.

decisions.why: *dealbábor* is a passive, 'I shall be whitened', and *super nivem* 'above the snow' (ὑπὲρ χιόνα) — the comparison. *ficarei mais branco do que a neve* says the comparison as Portuguese says it and keeps the whiteness and the snow; the passive agent is lost (it is God, named in *lavareis* just before). *branqueado* is laundry, and in the other Portuguese it is money-laundering. DRB 'I shall be made whiter than snow', MS1932 *me tornarei mais branco que a neve*.

options.label: ficarei mais branco do que a neve

forms.dealbabor: ficarei mais branco do que a neve

options.note: Ruling.

options.label: serei feito mais branco que a neve

forms.dealbabor: serei feito mais branco que a neve

options.note: keeps the passive (DRB 'made whiter'); heavier.

options.label: me tornarei mais branco que a neve

forms.dealbabor: me tornarei mais branco que a neve

decisions.why: The row *gáudium → júbilo* names this verse: *alegria* is lætítia's and both stand here, so they must differ; *gozo* is heard sexually in Brazil. D43 freed *júbilo* for gáudium by giving the *jubiláre* family *aclamar*. The blind reader of Ps 20 did not know *júbilo*; the Matins versicle (*V. Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam. R. Et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta*, Psalmi matutinum) makes this the most-heard place of the word.

options.label: júbilo
options.note: Ruling; the row (20:7, 29:12).

options.label: regozijo
options.note: free in the glossary; heavier.

options.label: gozo
options.note: MS1932; refused by the row (heard sexually).

decisions.latin: Cor mundum crea in me, Deus
decisions.why: The Latin fronts the object; it is the Lent I antiphon (*Cor mundum * crea in me Deus*, Tempora/Quad1-0) and a Preces versicle. Portuguese says the imperative first, and the colon then ends on *puro*, a paroxytone, with the vocative inside it. Fronted (*Um coração puro criai em mim, Deus*) it is sayable and keeps the Latin's emphasis, but ends on the monosyllable. mundus → *puro* (the adjective of the mundáre row); víscera → *entranhas* (the organ kept, rule 5; MS1932 *entranhas*, DRB 'bowels'); *ínnova* → *renovai*; rectus → *reto*.

options.label: Criai em mim, Deus, um coração puro

forms.cormundum: Criai em mim, {v12deus}, um coração puro

options.note: Ruling; MS1932's order.

options.label: Um coração puro criai em mim, Deus

forms.cormundum: Um coração puro criai em mim, {v12deus}

options.note: the Latin's order; the antiphon's intonation would fall on *Um coração puro*.

decisions.latin: Ne proícias me a fácie tua
decisions.why: The proícere row names this verse and pencils *Não me lanceis da vossa face*. But 2:3 took *lançar para longe de* after the stylist heard *lançar de* as a calque, and the same holds here; ἀπορρίψῃς is 'cast away'. *para longe* is supplied as there (D2: grammar), the face (fácies → face) kept. *lanceis* is safe (rule 3: *lancei* differs). It reads alone as a Preces versicle (*V. Ne projícias me a fácie tua*).

options.label: para longe da vossa face
options.note: Ruling; as 2:3.

options.label: da vossa face
options.note: the row's pencilled form; shorter, a calque.

options.label: (arremesseis) da vossa presença
options.note: MS1932 *Não me arremesses da tua presença* — the face turned into presence. Refused (the face is the Latin's image).

decisions.latin: et spíritum sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me
decisions.why: The DO Latin prints *spíritum sanctum tuum* in lower case, as it does *spíritum rectum* (12) and *spíritu principáli* (14): the psalm's three spirits are one word. A capital would decide for the Person of the Spirit, which the Christian reader hears anyway and the Latin leaves to him (rule 2: do not resolve what the Latin leaves open). MS1932 *o teu espírito santo*, lower case. auferre → *tirar* (D41).

options.label: espírito santo
options.note: Ruling; as the Latin prints it.

options.label: Espírito Santo
options.note: decides for the Person; the Portuguese convention for the name.

decisions.why: *Redde* is 'give back' (ἀπόδος). The réddere row's *pagar* is for paying vows and repaying (7:5, 21:26, 27:4) and is wrong here; this verse decides locally. *Restituí-me* is the liturgical word, but *restituí* is also 'I restored' (rule 3); D13 lets the enclitic save it, yet *restituí-me* can still be heard as a first-person reflexive at the head of a verse said alone (the Preces versicle *V. Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui*). *Devolvei-me* is plain, exact and safe (*devolvi* differs). MS1932 *Dá-me* drops the 'back'.

options.label: Devolvei-me
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: Restituí-me
options.note: allowed by D13 (enclitic); more liturgical; the homograph risk above.

options.label: Tornai a dar-me
options.note: DRB 'Restore unto me' in two verbs; longer.

options.label: Dai-me
options.note: MS1932 and DM1962; drops the *re-*.

decisions.why: *principális* is 'of a prince, chief, ruling' (L&S); the Greek is ἡγεμονικῷ, 'leading, sovereign'. *principal* in Portuguese means only 'main' and would be wrong; *soberano* is the plain word for a ruling spirit, one that governs. DRB 'perfect', MS1932 *magnânimo*, DM1962 (from the Hebrew, 'willing') *entusiasmo*. The Friday Lauds antiphon (*Spíritu principáli * confírma cor meum, Deus*) opens with the phrase.

options.label: soberano
options.note: Ruling; the Greek's sense.

options.label: de príncipe
options.note: keeps the Latin root's prince; a phrase where the Latin has an adjective.

options.label: magnânimo
options.note: MS1932; the greatness of soul, not the ruling.

options.label: generoso
options.note: the Hebrew's sense (נדיבה). Refused (rule 1).

decisions.why: The confirmáre row is open: with a person as object *confirmar* was heard at 36:17 as 'attest', and in a Catholic mouth *confirmai-me* is heard first as the sacrament. στήρισόν με is 'make firm, prop up'. The row's option *firmar* (already used for *confirmáre* in Ps 17's *firmastes sobre mim a vossa mão*) keeps the root and the image. *firmai* is safe (rule 3). The imperative comes first and the colon ends on the adjective; the Preces say it alone (*R. Et spíritu principáli confírma me*).

options.label: firmai-me
options.note: Ruling; the row's option.

options.label: confirmai-me
options.note: the cognate; heard as the sacrament or as 'attest'.

options.label: sustentai-me
options.note: 36:17's word for *confírmat justos*; loses the root.

options.label: fortalecei-me
options.note: MS1932 *conforta-me* nearby; *fortalecer* is confortáre's.

decisions.why: convértere → *voltar* is the row's verb; D25 made the exception *converter* where men are told to turn to God, because that sense is conversion and *voltar* can be heard as said of God. Here the ungodly turn to God — the same sense, said as a promise rather than a command — so the exception is extended. DRB 'shall be converted to thee', MS1932 *se converterão a ti*. The verse is the Quad5-2 responsory (*R. Docébo iníquos vias tuas: et ímpii ad te converténtur*). Proposed for the glossary as an extension of D25.

options.label: se converterão a vós
options.note: Ruling; D25 extended.

options.label: se voltarão para vós
options.note: the row's verb; loses the conversion the verse promises.

decisions.why: D29 rules the plural *sanguínes* → *sangue* in every place, and names this verse. *do sangue derramado* (DM1962) and MS1932's gloss (*o castigo … do sangue de Urias*) explain. liberáre → *livrar* (row).

options.label: do sangue
options.note: Ruling; D29; MS1932 *Livra-me do sangue*.

options.label: dos sangues
options.note: the Latin's plural (the Latinist's request in Ps 15); heard as a slip.

decisions.latin: et exsultábit lingua mea justítiam tuam
decisions.why: The Latin (and Greek, ἀγαλλιάσεται … τὴν δικαιοσύνην σου) makes *exsultáre* transitive: my tongue will exult your justice, i.e. exultantly tell it. Portuguese *exultar* takes no direct object. The verb is kept (the exsultáre row) and the relation given a preposition: *na vossa justiça* is the psalter's own (12:6b, 9:16a *exultar na vossa salvação*), which loses the telling-forth. MS1932 *exaltará* changes the verb; DRB 'extol' likewise. The bare transitive is offered for the readers to judge.

options.label: exultará na vossa justiça
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: exultará a vossa justiça
options.note: the Latin's transitive; strained Portuguese.

options.label: cantará com exultação a vossa justiça

forms.exsultabit: cantará com exultação a vossa justiça

options.note: keeps the object by adding a verb; adds a word the Latin lacks.

options.label: exaltará a vossa justiça
options.note: MS1932; another Latin verb (exaltáre). Refused.

decisions.why: delectári (deponent, 'take delight in') is *deleitar-se* in the finished 36:4 (*Deleita-te no Senhor*, a versicle). The causative *delectáre* at 29:2 went to *alegrar* because its Greek there is εὐφραίνω; here the Greek is εὐδοκήσεις ('be well pleased'), so that argument does not pull. Kept as 36:4. The Latin's future stays. Note: the same Greek verb returns in 50:21 as *acceptábis*; the Latin varies it with a word of another sense (accept), so the two stay two (*aceitareis*).

options.label: deleitareis
options.note: Ruling; = 36:4.

options.label: comprazereis
options.note: MS1932 *te comprazes*; bookish (the stylist, 25:3).

decisions.why: *contribuláre* is 'crush', figuratively 'afflict much' (L&S cites this verse); συντετριμμένον 'broken'. *atribulado* keeps the Latin root (*tribulátio → tribulação*) and the affliction; it is plain Brazilian. *contrito* is kept for *contrítum* in the next colon (the contérere row foresaw it), so the two Latin words stay two. MS1932 *compungido* (compúngere's), DRB 'afflicted'.

options.label: atribulado
options.note: Ruling; DRB 'afflicted'.

options.label: quebrantado
options.note: the Greek's 'broken'; *quebranto* is the evil eye in Brazil (the contrítio row).

options.label: compungido
options.note: MS1932; compúngere's word (4:5 *compungi-vos*).

decisions.why: The open row *despícere (God) → desdenhar* (9:22, 21:25, 26:9b) would give *não desdenhareis*. By D15's test it should not: at 21:25 *non sprevit, neque despéxit* the Greek is οὐκ ἐξουδένωσεν οὐδὲ προσώχθισεν, and *sprevit* (ἐξουδένωσεν) became *desprezou*; here *despícies* is ἐξουθενώσει — the very Greek verb of 21:25's *desprezou* (read in `consult/parallels/ps021.md` and this psalm's parallels). 9:22 (ὑπερορᾷς) and 26:9b are other verbs. So *desprezareis*. It is also the plain word, and the blind reader of Ps 9 did not know *desdenhais*. The Friday Lauds antiphon (*Cor contrítum * et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies*) ends on it.

options.label: desprezareis
options.note: Ruling; the Greek of 21:25's *desprezou*; DRB 'despise', MS1932 *desprezarás*.

options.label: desdenhareis
options.note: the open row's word (9:22, 21:25, 26:9b).

decisions.latin: Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion
decisions.why: *Benígne fac* is 'deal kindly' (ἀγάθυνον, 'do good to'), with *Sion* as its object. Portuguese has no light verb that takes the adverb well (*fazei benignamente a Sião* is not a sentence); the adverb becomes an adjective with the copula — grammar (D2), as MS1932 *sê benigno com Sião*. The Latin's order is kept, so that the antiphon (*Benígne fac, Dómine, * in bona voluntáte tua Sion*, Saturday Lauds) divides where it does: *Sede benigno, Senhor, * na vossa boa vontade, com Sião*. bona volúntas → *boa vontade* (row).

options.label: Sede benigno … com Sião

forms.benigne: Sede benigno, Senhor, na vossa boa vontade, com Sião

options.note: Ruling; MS1932's build.

options.label: Fazei bem … a Sião

forms.benigne: Fazei bem, Senhor, na vossa boa vontade, a Sião

options.note: the light verb kept (*fac*), the Greek's sense; *fazer bem a* is plain; the adverb's kindness becomes 'good'.

options.label: Tratai com bondade … Sião

forms.benigne: Tratai com bondade, Senhor, na vossa boa vontade, Sião

options.note: DRB 'Deal favourably'; *bondade* is bónitas's.

decisions.why: ædificáre → *edificar* (27:5). The present passive subjunctive as the pronominal passive, *se edifiquem* (MS1932), one of Portuguese's two passives and the lighter. The Latin says 'be built', not 'rebuilt' (DM1962 *reedifica*, from the Hebrew's context).

options.label: se edifiquem
options.note: Ruling; MS1932.

options.label: sejam edificados
options.note: the analytic passive; one syllable longer.

decisions.latin: tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos
decisions.why: impónere super → *pôr sobre* (*porão*; the subject unnamed, as the Latin). vítulus → *bezerro* (the row: *novilhos* was unknown to the blind reader of Ps 21; the row allowed *novilhos* here locally and I do not take it, so that one word serves the psalter). The Latin ends on *vítulos*; Portuguese puts the object before the place and ends on *altar*. *porão* is also the noun 'hold, basement'; in a verb slot after *então* it should not be heard so — the readers will say.

options.label: porão bezerros sobre o vosso altar

forms.imponent: porão bezerros sobre o vosso altar

choices.50:3a: miseréri → *ter piedade* (formula *Miserére mei → Tende piedade de mim*); misericórdia → *misericórdia*. The incipit, sung as the Monday Lauds antiphon (*Miserére * mei, Deus, secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam*) and the Asperges psalm verse (Ordo/Prayers). *grande* before the noun, as the Latin's *magnam*.
choices.50:3b: delére → *apagar* (the commínuere / delére row names 50:3b and 50:11). The Tuesday Lauds antiphon *Dele iniquitátem meam, Dómine* reads from the second colon. *compaixões* is an oxytone at the mediant; allowed (rule 4). Length -4: *multidão das vossas compaixões* is shorter than the Latin genitives.
choices.50:4: iníquitas → *iniquidade*, peccátum → *pecado*: the psalm's two sin-words are kept two throughout (3b, 4, 5, 7, 11), as the Latin and the Greek (ἀνομία / ἁμαρτία).
choices.50:5: *ego cognósco*: the emphatic *ego* kept as *eu*; cognóscere → *conhecer* (row). *sempre* moves before the place, the Portuguese order.
choices.50:6: *malum coram te feci* → *e fiz o mal diante de vós*; coram → *diante de*. The first colon reads alone as the Thursday Lauds antiphon. *justificado … julgado*: an internal echo, the Latin's own (*justificéris … judicáris*); not at a mark. Length +6 in the second colon: *para que sejais* and *quando fordes* are the subjunctives Portuguese spells in full.
choices.50:7: The Latin plurals *iniquitátibus*, *peccátis* kept plural; *em pecados me concebeu a minha mãe* keeps the parallel fronting of the two phrases, and ends on *mãe* as the Latin on *mater mea*.
choices.50:9: The Asperges antiphon (with *Dómine*: *Vós me aspergireis, Senhor, com o hissopo …*). The Latin's future is kept against the memory of an imperative in Portuguese use (not verified, and not the Latin). Length +8/+4 (checks): the two named subjects and the Portuguese future and comparison; the subjects are kept so each colon stands alone (see `asperges`, option 3 is one syllable shorter).
choices.50:10: audítus → *ouvido* (the sense of hearing); *Ao meu ouvido dareis* keeps the Latin's build against DM1962's *Faze-me ouvir* (from the Hebrew). humiliáre → *humilhar* (row); ossa → *ossos*. The second colon stands alone as the Matins response and in the Office of the Dead antiphon (*Exsultábunt Dómino * ossa humiliáta*, Commune/C9).
choices.50:11: avértere fáciem → *desviar a face* (row, the formula of 12:1, 26:9). Both cola are Preces versicle and response.
choices.50:12: Both cola are Preces versicle and response; see `cormundum`, `deus`.
choices.50:13: Both cola are Preces versicle and response.
choices.50:14: salutáre → *salvação* (D6); lætítia → *alegria*. The psalm's three spirits (12, 13, 14) and the fourth (19) are all *espírito*. Both cola are Preces versicle and response.
choices.50:15: docére → *ensinar*; iníquus / ímpius → *iníquo / ímpio* (row: kept distinct). Future *Ensinarei* as the Latin. *vós* at the final: a stressed monosyllable, allowed (rule 4). Length +5: *aos iníquos os vossos caminhos* spells the articles Latin lacks; nothing to cut.
choices.50:16: salus → *salvação* (D6); *Deus, Deus da minha salvação* as 37:23 *Senhor, Deus da minha salvação*. The first colon is the Quad5-2 responsory's respond and reads alone. Length -5: *sanguínibus* (5 syllables) is *sangue* (2) by D29.
choices.50:17: The opening versicle of the Office (Psalterium/Common/Prayers.txt *[Domine labia]*: *V. Dómine, lábia ++ mea apéries. R. Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.*) — each colon reads alone: *Senhor, abrireis os meus lábios. — E a minha boca anunciará o vosso louvor.* *apéries* is a future and stays one; the bare imperative *Abri os meus lábios* is also barred by rule 3 (*abri* = 'I opened'). annuntiáre → *anunciar* (D41); laus → *louvor*.
choices.50:18: *sacrifícium* without article, as 39:7 *Não quisestes sacrifício*; *dedíssem útique* → *eu certamente o teria dado* (the pronoun supplies the object Portuguese needs). holocáustum → *holocausto* (row).
choices.50:19: The copula supplied in the verbless first colon (D2). contrítum → *contrito* (the contérere row foresaw it); humiliátum → *humilhado*. The second colon is the Friday Lauds antiphon. Rhyme flag 50:18/19 (*deleitareis / desprezareis*): the Latin's two second-person futures (*delectáberis / despícies*), in the same place; kept.
choices.50:20: Sion → *Sião*; Jerúsalem → *Jerusalém*. *Sião* at the mediant and *Jerusalém* at the final are both oxytones: the names.
choices.50:21: sacrifícium justítiæ → *sacrifício de justiça* (4:6); oblátio → *oferenda* (D41); holocáustum → *holocausto*. *acceptáre* → *aceitar*. The Quad4-0 antiphon (*Tunc acceptábis * sacrifícium justítiæ …*) reads. Articles supplied before the list (Portuguese wants them after *o sacrifício*); *tunc … tunc* kept as *Então … então*.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm50.txt, 20 prayed verses (50:3a–50:21; DO's ids begin at 3, tituli out by D7). No flex; one mediant per verse. Liturgical uses found by grep (ps032/uses.py): the whole psalm at ferial Lauds (Psalmi major, Day0 Laudes2 and DayaC Laudes2 by reference ;;50) with antiphons from 3a, 3b, 4, 6a, 14b, 19b, 20a (Days 1–6 and the Monastic/Cistercian series); 50:17 the opening versicle of the Office (Common/Prayers.txt [Domine labia]); 50:11–14 as four versicle/response pairs in the Sunday Prime Preces (Special/Preces.txt); 50:9 the Asperges antiphon, with 50:3a as its psalm verse (missa Ordo/Prayers); 50:10 the Matins versicle (Psalmi matutinum); 50:10b the Office of the Dead Lauds antiphon (Commune/C9); 50:12 Lent I antiphon (Quad1-0); 50:15–17 the Quad5-2 responsory; 50:21 + 50:11 the Quad4-0 antiphon; 50:5–6 versicles (Pent01-3, Epi2-0); the whole psalm in OrdoA.txt ('the priest recites Psalms 50 and 42 on the way to the altar'). 50:6b = Rom 3:4 (Clementine, consult/bolls-VULG-45-3.json, fetched earlier). The Office of the Dead use of the whole psalm was not verified beyond the C9 antiphon.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps050.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Rulings applied: D2, D3 n/a, D6 (*salvação* 14, 16), D15 (*palavras* 6), D29 (*do sangue* 16), D41 (*oferenda* 21), D13 (enclitic imperatives; see `redde`), rule 3 (50:17 future kept; *firmai*, *lanceis*, *devolvei* safe). Rows applied: miseréri, misericórdia, miseratiónes, multitúdo, delére, iníquitas, mundáre (purificar, and why not *limpar*), cognóscere, ecce / enim (= 53:6), dilígere, véritas, gáudium (*júbilo*), humiliáre, avértere fáciem, proícere, auferre, salutáre, docére, ímpius / iníquus, liberáre, annuntiáre, laus, holocáustum, contérere (*contrito*), bona volúntas, ædificáre, vítulus. Departures proposed for the glossary: *despícere* at 50:19 → *desprezar* (D15's Greek test against the open *desdenhar* row), *convértere* → *converter* (D25's exception extended), *réddere* 'give back' → *devolver*, *confirmáre* → *firmar* with persons, *principális* → *soberano*, *contribuláre* → *atribulado*, *delectári* → *deleitar-se* (= 36:4), *incértus* → *incerto*, *contra me* (facing) → *diante de mim*. Lines said alone checked: 3a, 3b (antiphon), 6a, 9, 10a/10b, 11a/11b, 12a/12b, 13a/13b, 14a/14b, 15, 16a, 17a/17b, 19b, 20a, 21a.

render.py and checks.py run: hard checks pass (ids, one * per verse). Soft flags accepted in choices: lengths 50:3b, 5, 6, 8, 9, 15, 16, 17, 20 (article and subjunctive expansion; D29 shortens 16); neighbouring finals rhyme 50:18/19 (-eis, the Latin's parallel futures).
